messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Commitment pathway for isolated GPU pool — StraitHealth

Hi Michael — thanks again for taking time today. I promised to send a concise write-up capturing the pain points we heard, the success criteria you shared, and a practical next-step plan so your procurement and infra teams can move quickly. TL;DR: StraitHealth is a fit for a dedicated (isolated) GPU pool with a staged scaling runway and SLOs we can commit to.

Key pain points we heard
- Inference latency variability with multi-tenant endpoints leading to inconsistent user experience for clinicians.
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI on isolated hardware; auditability for access & billing is mandatory.
- Predictable monthly spend to budget for the next fiscal year.

Goals & success criteria (as you described)
1) Isolated GPU pool with tenant-level separation and private network access (VPC).
2) 99th-percentile inference latency <= 250ms for 512-token requests during peak windows.
3) Ability to scale from 4->16 GPU units over an initial 3 month ramp without downtime.
4) Audit logs and key management (customer-managed KMS) for all inference sessions.
5) Procurement prefers a 12-month reserved capacity commitment with one 3-month opt-in burst window.

High-level proposed path (what Redwood will deliver)
- Phase 0 (Prep, 1 week): finalize SOW + security checklist; exchange network diagrams and enable KMS integration.
- Phase 1 (Provision, 2–3 weeks): stand up isolated pool in us-west-2, run acceptance tests targeted at the 99p latency SLO.
- Phase 2 (Pilot, 4 weeks): route a small percentage of traffic, enable prefix caching + quantization profile to hit cost targets.
- Phase 3 (Ramp, 8–12 weeks): scale up GPUs to committed level and enable autoscaling policies + burst window.

SLOs we propose to commit in the contract
- Availability SLA: 99.5% for the isolated pool (monthly).
- Performance SLO: 99th percentile latency <= 250ms for 512-token requests under the agreed workload profile.
- Response time for critical incidents: 1 hour (pager) with an on-call rotation.

Open questions for your team
- Final committed GPU count desired for month 1 (we sketched 8 as the midpoint).
- Any additional compliance paperwork beyond SOC2 + customer-managed KMS (e.g., specific attestation required by your audit team).
- Preferred billing cadence (monthly invoice vs. net-30 consolidated quarterly).

Attached: SOW-draft-v1.pdf (skeleton with commercial terms), isolation-network-sketch.png (diagram to align on VPC peering).

Next steps (proposed)
1) Michael / Procurement: confirm initial committed GPUs for month 1 and preferred billing cadence by 9/10.
2) Redwood: update SOW with the committed quantity and compliance appendix; share final SOW for signature.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical runbook call with Andrew in your infra team and Marcus (ops) — propose 9/14 or 9/15.

If you want, I can convert the SOW into a PDF with the pricing table (ballpark) for Procurement to evaluate.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this into ops.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com

Michael — great questions, answers inline below.

1) Ballpark pricing: for an 8-GPU reserved pool (NVIDIA A800-equivalent) with the isolation and audit controls we discussed, estimated committed monthly spend is USD 68,000 — this includes support (standard SLA) and 1 emergency burst window per quarter. I'll add a 3-tier pricing table (4 / 8 / 16 GPUs) to the SOW and send by EOD 9/10. This is a not-to-exceed figure for Procurement's evaluation; final contract will reflect exact quantities and any discounts.

2) KMS & audit logs: yes — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (we'll integrate with your KMS and can forward key-rotation and access logs to your audit bucket). We'll add the KMS appendix to the SOW and a short integration checklist.

3) KV cache isolation: this is supported as a configuration. For strict tenant KV separation we will enable per-tenant cache namespaces and ensure the runtime enforces namespace boundaries; no code changes required for the common model families. We'll document the configuration in the ops runbook.

Next logistical items I will take on now:
- Update SOW with a pricing table for 4 / 8 / 16 GPUs + KMS appendix (deliverable: updated SOW pdf).
- Pull in Ops (Marcus) to prepare a technical runbook draft and acceptance test plan.
- Propose 9/14 10:00–10:30 PT for the technical runbook call; if that works I'll send a calendar invite.

If Procurement wants a shorter term to start (e.g., 3-month trial) with conversion to a 12-month reserved contract, we can draft that option in the commercial terms.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the updated SOW.

Best,
Grace
